concerns.text: The plan tests the null hypothesis that φ(n) mod p is uniformly distributed (Section ‘Summary’ and Research ‘Problem Definition’). However, number‑theoretic results (e.g., φ(n) ≡ 0 (mod p) for n divisible by p² or by any prime q ≡ 1 (mod p)) prove that uniformity is false for all primes p. Thus the research question is mathematically disproven a priori, making the planned χ² test a trivial confirmation of a known theorem rather than an empirical discovery. This constitutes a science‑level defect.

The plan introduces a ‘theoretical bias band’ based on the golden‑ratio constant φ ≈ 1.618 and ±φ√N (Research ‘Methodological Approach’). This band is not derived from any established result on the distribution of φ(n) residues and appears ad‑hoc. Using it as a validation criterion creates a circular/unsupported justification for observed deviations and is not an accepted statistical or number‑theoretic method.
